svg.title: A cold front sweeps the Northeast coast — wind barbs pivot 180° and freshen to a gale behind it
svg.desc: Synoptic surface wind-barb station plot over the US Northeast seaboard and adjacent western Atlantic. Each station is a wind barb whose staff points from the wind and whose ticks tally speed in knots: a filled pennant is 50 knots, a full barb 10 knots, a half barb 5 knots. Ahead of the blue cold front a warm southwesterly flow (orange) streams up the coast at 20 to 40 knots; behind it a cold northwesterly gale (blue) reaches 45 to 50 knots, the staffs having pivoted roughly 180 degrees across the front.
svg.text: A cold front swings the wind hard around the coast
Surface analysis · warm southwesterly ahead of the front, a cold northwesterly gale filling in behind — barb ticks tally knots
How to read a wind barb
Staff points from the wind; ticks tally the speed.
teeth point the way it moves
